points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once (a single time), not on each function call.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.75 if only says it is initialized/allocated once without contrasting with non-static.

points.description: States that a static array retains/persists its contents (values) between function calls, i.e. its lifetime is the whole program run.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.75 for a vague statement such as 'it remembers/keeps its values' without mention of calls or lifetime.

points.description: States that a non-static (automatic/local) array is created and re-initialized every time the function is called, and its contents are lost when the function exits.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.75 if only one of: re-initialized each call, or destroyed/lost on exit.

points.description: Gives a supporting detail on storage or default behaviour, e.g. static array is stored in static/data memory (not the stack), is zero-initialized by default, or its scope remains local to the function while the lifetime is program-long; non-static array is on the stack with indeterminate values if uninitialized.
